root.name: King's Indian Defense: Exchange Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 e5 7. dxe5

overview: White resolves the tension at once with 7.dxe5 dxe5 8.Qxd8 Rxd8 9.Bg5, trading queens and heading for a quiet endgame-like middlegame. White has a slightly freer game and a target on Black's e5 pawn and the d-file; Black develops with ...Re8, ...c6 or ...Nbd7, using the bishop on g7 and a solid pawn on e5. There is no pawn storm and few attacks; the game is a manoeuvring fight for small edges, famously drawish.

white_ideas.idea: Use the half-open d-file and the d5 square; Nd5 to hit the weak c7 pawn
Play Bg5, Nd5 and O-O-O or Rd1 to pressure Black's position
Trade pieces and aim for an edge in space with e4 and c4 held

black_ideas.idea: Hold the centre with ...Re8, ...c6 and ...Nbd7 and bring the bishop to ...e6 or ...Bf8
Meet Nd5 by ...Nxd5 or ...c6; keep the e5 pawn defended
Neutralise the queenless middlegame and head for a draw or a long manoeuvring game

typical_structures.structure: Queenless middlegame with White pawns c4/e4 against Black e5 and c7; open d-file

character.notes: Queens are off early and neither side has a direct attack; Black is hard to break. Solid.

gambit.notes: The e5 pawn is recaptured at once.

structure.notes: A symmetrical-ish exchange structure with an open d-file. Semi-open.

approach.notes: A well-known main-line sideline played by strong players. Standard.

level.notes: Plans such as the Nd5 and the ...c6 set-up are simple, but the endgame needs technique. Intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: 9.Bg5 Re8 10.Nd5
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 e5 7. dxe5 dxe5 8. Qxd8 Rxd8 9. Bg5 Re8 10. Nd5
sublines_that_differ.how: White puts a knight on d5 and aims at c7.

sublines_that_differ.name: 9.Bg5 c6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 e5 7. dxe5 dxe5 8. Qxd8 Rxd8 9. Bg5 c6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black prevents Nd5 with a solid pawn on c6.

character.reason: Early queen trade and a compact Black position with no forcing play.

structure.reason: A fixed exchange structure with a half-open d-file; Flexible is the alternative.

approach.reason: A mainstream line against the King's Indian.

level.reason: Not the full King's Indian race, but the queenless plans need judgement.

plans.reason: Nd5 is White's main idea and Black fights to prevent or exchange it.
